### Executive Summary
- Actively exploited Chrome zero‑day (CVE‑2026‑2441) and a critical BeyondTrust domain‑takeover vuln are now priority patch/hunt items; CISA ordered 72h remediation for BeyondTrust.
- Multiple campaigns abusing remote access (ScreenConnect phishing), Outlook/Office add‑ins and DNS‑based delivery (ClickFix) increase initial access risk for endpoints and email.
- Ransomware (LockBit 5.0, BridgePay‑linked incidents, healthcare/hospital outages) remains highly active across Windows, Linux, and ESXi – reinforce controls on privileged access and hypervisors.

---

### High-priority items (immediate attention)

- **Chrome zero‑day – CVE‑2026‑2441 exploited in the wild**  
  • What happened: Google released an emergency patch for a Chrome zero‑day being actively exploited (multiple sources).  
  • Why it matters: Browser RCE is a common entry vector for drive‑by and phishing‑linked intrusions on user workstations and admin laptops.  
  • Recommended immediate actions: Confirm enterprise Chrome/Chromium‑based browsers auto‑update is enabled and working; start checking EDR for suspicious browser‑spawned processes and new child binaries from Chrome today.

- **BeyondTrust privilege escalation – active exploitation & CISA 72h directive (CVE‑2026‑1731)**  
  • What happened: Critical BeyondTrust flaw is being exploited in the wild; CISA ordered US agencies to patch within 72 hours.  
  • Why it matters: Successful exploitation can lead to full domain control via compromised PAM infrastructure.  
  • Recommended immediate actions: Inventory any BeyondTrust products (on‑prem or SaaS); verify patch/mitigation status today; if exposed, pull VPN/firewall logs for anomalous access to those hosts and hunt for unusual directory/privileged account activity around them.

- **ScreenConnect misuse via phishing (“fake Social Security emails”)**  
  • What happened: Campaigns are abusing ScreenConnect remote access links delivered via convincing social‑themed phishing to hijack PCs.  
  • Why it matters: Remote support tools can provide instant, high‑privilege interactive access bypassing standard malware patterns.  
  • Recommended immediate actions: Tighten email detections for ScreenConnect/remote‑tool URLs; monitor for new ScreenConnect agents/installers; flag any outbound ScreenConnect sessions from endpoints not used by IT support.

- **LockBit 5.0 and ongoing ransomware activity (BridgePay, hotel, hospital cases)**  
  • What happened: LockBit 5.0 now targets Windows, Linux, ESXi; multiple organizations (payments provider, hotel, hospital) reported ransomware‑linked or “network disruption” incidents.  
  • Why it matters: Multi‑platform lockers directly threaten banking back‑office, Linux app servers and hypervisors hosting critical financial systems.  
  • Recommended immediate actions: Review EDR for known pre‑ransom behaviors (mass LSASS access, shadow copy deletion, suspicious ESXi commands); confirm recent backups and hypervisor hardening; ensure response runbooks and isolation procedures are immediately accessible.

- **Office/Outlook add‑ins & ClickFix DNS‑based delivery**  
  • What happened: Reports of Outlook add‑ins being hijacked plus a “ClickFix” attack chain abusing nslookup/DNS lookups to fetch RAT payloads.  
  • Why it matters: These are low‑friction vectors on user workstations that can bypass traditional email attachment scanning and use living‑off‑the‑land binaries.  
  • Recommended immediate actions: Hunt for nslookup / curl / powershell / certutil invoked by Office processes (WINWORD/OUTLOOK/EXCEL) in the last 7 days; monitor for new or changed Outlook add‑ins, especially from non‑standard paths.

---

### Monitoring & detection recommendations

- **Browser zero‑day & drive‑by attacks (Chrome CVE‑2026‑2441)**  
  • Logs: EDR, web proxy, DNS.  
  • Hunt for Chrome spawning scripting interpreters or LOLBins (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, wscript.exe, mshta.exe) and immediate outbound C2 (ATT&CK T1203, T1059).

- **BeyondTrust / PAM exploitation**  
  • Logs: BeyondTrust application logs, Windows Security logs on domain controllers, VPN/firewall logs around PAM servers.  
  • Look for new privileged accounts, unexpected group membership changes, unusual logons to DCs from PAM hosts, and interactive logins at odd hours (T1068, T1078).

- **Remote access abuse (ScreenConnect & similar tools)**  
  • Logs: Endpoint app inventory/EDR, proxy, firewall, email gateway.  
  • Alert on installation or execution of ScreenConnect, AnyDesk, TeamViewer, etc. on non‑IT endpoints; watch for outbound connections to new ScreenConnect/cloud‑RMM domains (T1105, T1219).

- **Office/Outlook add‑ins and ClickFix DNS‑based delivery**  
  • Logs: EDR, DNS logs, Office 365 audit logs (if applicable).  
  • Hunt for Office processes issuing high‑volume nslookup or unusual DNS queries and dropping binaries/scripts to temp directories; alert on new or disabled security add‑ins (T1204, T1059, T1071.004).

- **Ransomware staging and execution (LockBit 5.0, current incidents)**  
  • Logs: EDR, Windows event logs, ESXi/hypervisor logs, backup system logs.  
  • Monitor for: mass file modifications, shadow copy deletions (vssadmin, wmic), ESXi shell commands that snapshot/unregister VMs, sudden backup failure spikes (T1486, T1490).

- **Malicious GitHub / open‑source supply chain**  
  • Logs: Developer endpoints, CI/CD, proxy logs for github.com and package registries.  
  • Flag `git clone` / package install from unknown repos into production‑adjacent systems; watch for build servers spawning network scanners or credential dumpers shortly after pulling new code (T1195, T1552).

- **WordPress/Joomla and web‑app plugin vulns (CleanTalk, Novarain/Tassos, FileZen)**  
  • Logs: WAF, web server logs, CMS logs.  
  • Look for spikes in unusual parameters, SQLi‑like patterns, and direct requests to plugin paths; monitor for unexpected admin logins or file uploads (T1190, T1505).

- **Mobile spyware / ZeroDayRAT (Android/iOS)**  
  • Logs: MDM/EAM, VPN, IdP.  
  • Watch for new, unapproved mobile apps on corporate devices, sudden new VPN endpoints from unusual geos, or repeated MFA prompts indicating device compromise (T1404, T1430 – mobile).

---

### Medium-term follow-ups

- **Patch management: browsers & privileged systems**  
  • Ensure Chrome/Edge and other Chromium browsers are in a rapid update ring; verify all BeyondTrust, VPN, File transfer (FileZen) and PAM systems are on latest patches and removed from direct internet exposure where possible.

- **Remote‑tool governance**  
  • Formalize policy on allowed remote access tools (ScreenConnect, RMMs); enforce via application control and proxy allowlists; add periodic reviews to detect shadow IT remote tools.

- **Ransomware resilience review**  
  • Re‑validate RTO/RPO and offline backup coverage for core banking, payments, SWIFT, trading platforms, and ESXi clusters; test restore procedures at least in tabletop if not live.

- **Email and collaboration hardening**  
  • Tighten controls on Outlook/Office add‑ins (allow‑list trusted publishers); revisit phishing training with emphasis on “remote help” lures and fake government/benefits emails.

- **Developer and supply‑chain security**  
  • Brief dev/DevOps on the active malicious GitHub repo campaign and open‑source registry funding/risks; enforce pinned dependencies and repository allow‑listing for build pipelines.

- **AI/agent and SSRF protections (LangChain SSRF, OpenClaw discussions)**  
  • For any internal AI/agent deployments or API‑driven microservices, review network egress rules, metadata service access, and SSRF mitigations (input validation, IMDSv2, service‑to‑service allow‑lists).
